acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction with a large receipt journal shows `pool confirm-safe` no longer decodes the full receipt history under taskman.prepare.lock: either it builds on the writer checkpoint (as `queue status` does) or the history read happens before lock acquisition with a revalidation under the lock; a focused test or benchmark pins the bound (e.g. receipts decoded or lock hold time independent of journal length).

Concurrent heartbeat/claim during confirm-safe no longer exceeds the 30 s preparation acquisition on the reproduction; existing pool safe-reuse semantics (V1-0695, V1-0674) are preserved; GH #701 is closed with the evidence.
body: beamfall/corvint#701 (2026-10-09, corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.0, Corvint main a5527cf42, macOS, ~10 concurrent clients). With a queue of about 21,100 receipts (.git/taskman 265 MB, writer-checkpoint 1.4 MB), `corvint-tasks pool confirm-safe --member lane-3` ran for more than 4 min at ~22% CPU. It was the only holder of taskman.prepare.lock and prepare.slot.00. A sample was dominated by wire parser, journal.Reader.step and snapshot.DecodeReceipt, which is a full journal decode rather than a checkpoint-based one. `queue status` takes 0.61 s by comparison. Concurrent confirm-safe, claim and heartbeat calls failed with LOCK_TIMEOUT after 30 s (rank=3, then rank=8). A caller timeout killed confirm-safe at 240 s before commit, so the lane stayed QUARANTINED and the work was lost. Expected: confirm-safe derives state from the writer checkpoint as queue status does, completes in seconds, and does not hold the prepare lock while decoding history. Entry point: internal/tasks/cli/lease.go.

completion.reason: Merged in beamfall/corvint#702 (merge b2a0b8c6), fixing GitHub issue 701: pool confirm-safe now takes the writer-checkpoint route (CAL-V0-205, decision 0471); focused tests, doc gates, independent review PASS, CEM sealed. Live 21,100-receipt qualification NOT_RUN.

title: GH #701: pool confirm-safe replays the full receipt journal while holding taskman.prepare.lock, starving heartbeats/claims with LOCK_TIMEOUT
